evidence_claims.claim: Grounded circuit conductor and equipment grounding conductor have distinct definitions

supports.location: Grounded conductor versus equipment grounding conductor definitions

evidence_claims.limitations: OSHA is workplace regulation; IEC abstract does not certify a clause.

evidence_claims.claim: Neutral carries ordinary current and can develop voltage due to its impedance
evidence_claims.limitations: 0.2 ohm and 15 A example is a simplifying assumed circuit.

evidence_claims.claim: Intentionally grounded neutral is not generally safe to touch; open neutral may remain energized
evidence_claims.limitations: Actual fault topology varies; not a universal neutral-voltage prediction.

evidence_claims.claim: Equipment grounding/PE can provide protective current route and bonding reference
evidence_claims.limitations: Specific performance requires fault-loop and equipment design review.

evidence_claims.claim: Earth electrode resistance can make an earth-only fault loop inadequate for prompt breaker clearing

supports.location: Fault loop impedance and RCD rationale

evidence_claims.limitations: 25 ohm example only; actual earth impedance complex and local rules differ.

evidence_claims.claim: Earthing, bonding and protective disconnection are different functions
evidence_claims.limitations: Neither page alone validates specific system design.

evidence_claims.claim: TN source-related protective route differs from TT electrode-protective arrangement
evidence_claims.limitations: Single vendor guide; full applicable normative clauses not reviewed.

evidence_claims.claim: TT systems commonly require RCD for effective fault disconnection given earth-loop impedance

supports.location: TT source and installation electrode discussion
Ground-fault interrupter functions in US context

evidence_claims.limitations: No universal RCD type, trip threshold or application prescribed.

evidence_claims.claim: IT systems often use insulation monitoring and defined response to first and second fault
evidence_claims.limitations: No independent primary clause-level verification for specific IT protection thresholds.

evidence_claims.claim: TN-C-S includes combined PEN upstream and separate PE/N downstream
evidence_claims.limitations: Two Schneider sources not independent; locally adopted scheme required.

evidence_claims.claim: Open PEN can elevate exposed metal and undermine intended fault reference

supports.location: PEN carries protective and neutral function

evidence_claims.limitations: Specific open-PEN exposure mechanisms and mitigations require independent domain expert review.

evidence_claims.claim: Rejoining PE and N downstream can create unwanted normal-current parallel paths
evidence_claims.limitations: Bonding exceptions and exact points are system and code dependent.

evidence_claims.claim: Shared-neutral circuit with neutral open may divide 240 V across unlike loads
evidence_claims.limitations: Classroom topology only; real fault may include other paths.

evidence_claims.claim: Conductor color is jurisdiction- and edition-specific, not proof of conductor function
evidence_claims.limitations: Historical modifications and local color requirements need investigation.

evidence_claims.claim: RCD residual imbalance alone does not detect every dangerous voltage or open PEN

supports.location: Interpretation describes some GFCI open-neutral failures

evidence_claims.limitations: RCD model-specific behavior varies; open-PEN claims await expert review.

evidence_claims.claim: Alternative sources can change neutral reference and bonding configuration
evidence_claims.limitations: Inverter/transfer design requires model-specific documents; no field guidance validated.

description: Addresses topics from the lecture, including "Neutral is part of the circuit" and "A protective conductor has a different assignment".
